chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan and Fadalah, from Husayn, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who doubted while standing, not knowing whether he had bowed or not. He said: 'He bows and prostrates.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do in prayer if they doubt whether they have bowed?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) in cases of doubt during prayer, specifically when the worshipper is still standing. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that the doubt is resolved by assuming the ruku' was performed, requiring the worshipper to complete the bowing and then perform *sujud al-shakk* (prostration of doubt) to validate the prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential preference for stability in worship actions over frequent re-performance when uncertainty arises in the standing position.
